statusText: Tail risk low after the overnight upside push was fully retraced; mapped policy state EA_ON with elevated Stress.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band because the extension to 31,072.50 was fully retraced back to mid-band, VIX decayed from an intraday 16.46 to a 15.41 close, and long-end yields pulled back from 24-year highs. Elevated Stress reflects the unresolved AI revenue repricing, a crude supply premium and Asian equity weakness. The narrow checkpoint is 13:30-15:00 UTC, covering the cash open and the Michigan preliminary release.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures retrace an overnight push as Asia weakens and yields ease
body: December NQ futures trade 30,981.75, up 0.04%, inside a 30,953.00-31,072.50 evening band, with a second independent delayed quote at 30,993.50 confirming the level. The band's 31,072.50 high was extended and then fully retraced back to mid-band, so no session-extreme holding and no failed-retracement sequence is observed. December ES trades 7,826.75, up 0.13%, inside a 16-point band. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed 30,725.81, down 1.39%, after a 30,556.40-31,125.13 range, ending 169 points above its low; the S&P 500 closed 7,765.36, down 0.5%, and the Dow closed 51,231.64, up 0.1%. VIX settled 15.41, up 2.19%, after fading an intraday 16.46 high, which is a low absolute level for a 1.39% index decline and indicates volatility decay rather than expansion. The 10-year yield eased to 5.231% and the 30-year to about 5.60%, both back from 24-year highs of 5.364% and 5.7041%, after a $22 billion 30-year auction cleared 5.618% with indirect bidders taking 72.3%; the 2-year was 4.77% in the latest H.15 release. The driver of the decline was a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualised revenue is near $50 billion rather than the roughly $70 billion investors had inferred, which cut the Philadelphia semiconductor index 3.4%, with Oracle down more than 5%, AMD nearly 4% and Nvidia nearly 3%. Crude eased overnight to about 90.87 WTI and 103.60 Brent after settling 3.6% and 4.1% higher on Hurricane Isaias, now a Category 2 storm forecast ashore on the northern Gulf Coast late Friday, and on Iran's still-open review of the US response to its seven-day Strait of Hormuz reopening proposal. In Asia, the Nikkei 225 trades 68,249.51, down 1.15%, a divergence from flat NQ futures that reduces directional conviction rather than establishing a one-way path. Tail therefore stays in the low band while the breadth of unresolved catalysts keeps Stress elevated. The shared Finviz context file was 9 days old and marked partial, so it was treated as stale and not used; this assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail held 11-14 through the Asia hours of 8 October with Stress in the high 40s to low 50s, stepped into the watch band at the 07:00 UTC European handover and ran 20-23 through the European and early US session as the AI-led decline developed. The 17:00 UTC hour was the single elevated reading at Tail 28 with Stress 72 while the semiconductor drop was steepest. Tail then decayed to 17-18 from 20:00 UTC as the cash session recovered off its low and volatility failed to expand, with Confidence steady at 85-89 throughout.
outlookSummary: The conditional path keeps Tail in the low band through the Asia hours, easing to 15 around the 03:00-04:00 UTC lull, then steps into the watch band at the 07:00 UTC European handover on the prior session's analogue rather than on observed structure. Tail runs 20-21 through the European session and peaks at 23 in the 14:00 UTC Michigan preliminary hour, inside the narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC danger window that also covers the cash open. Base case is decay back to the low band from 16:00 UTC on orderly two-way discovery, a brief watch-band return for the Friday final hour and the 20:00 UTC cash close alongside a scheduled Fed Collins speech, then a low-band 13-14 through the weekend futures halt. Confidence declines from 88 to 81 across the horizon. Gulf Coast landfall and the open Hormuz review are tracked as weekend gap exposure, not as intraday Tail.
